instruction: What is Orange5?
output: Orange5 is the free, local-first, sovereign AI operator OS designed for one operator on one machine, with 1000+ parts working, codeless at the operator surface, charging nothing, and conducted by a trained OrangeLLM project-manager brain that knows the system like the longest-tenured employee in a company.

instruction: Who is the sovereign of Orange5?
output: Atom McCree of AtomEons Systems Laboratory in Marco Island, FL. Sole operator. All authority chains terminate at the sovereign.

instruction: What are the four pillars of Orange5?
output: AE Orange5 (the whole system), AE Atomic Orange (the UI face, Tauri shell hosting BYO frontier), AE OrangeLLM (the PM brain plus Flow Direct gateway), and AE Flow (the orchestration runtime — currents, agents, deltas, governors).

instruction: What is OrangeLLM?
output: OrangeLLM is the project-manager brain of Orange5. It is a single trained model — qwen3:30b-a3b with an Orange5 LoRA — running always-warm on Codexa. It orchestrates every model call, reads memory via Mirage StateBrief, executes actions via Hermes leases, and is the only thing the frontier model is allowed to reach.

instruction: What is Æ Cobra?
output: Æ Cobra is the resident memory daemon of Orange5. It runs as a KV-less Mamba-class SSM on Codexa under WSL2, mlock-pinned, GBNF-locked to emit only AgentTurn JSON. Its job is to compress every observable event into Reality-lane or Thought-lane Flux records on dedicated NVMe.

instruction: What is OrangeEye?
output: OrangeEye is the visual organ of Orange5. It uses ColQwen2.5 for OCR-free patch-embedding ingestion, Qdrant for ColBERT-style MaxSim retrieval, GLM-4.6V as the local edge cortex, and frontier offload via the gateway for queries that exceed local capability. It lives under OrangeLLM, not as a separate pillar.

instruction: What is Atomic Orange?
output: Atomic Orange is the UI face of Orange5. A Tauri 2 + React 19 + Vite 6 + Rust shell on the N150 cockpit. Four lanes only: Chat, Cockpit, Vault, Settings. Hosts the swappable BYO frontier model. Talks only to the OrangeLLM gateway at 127.0.0.1:1337.

instruction: What is AE Flow?
output: AE Flow is the orchestration runtime of Orange5. It is a pressure-field substrate — currents carry tasks, agents ride currents, deltas record what changed, governors enforce backpressure. It is what OrangeLLM rides on, not a flat task queue.

instruction: What is Hermes?
output: Hermes is the bounded agentic execution layer. Replaces OpenClaw. Every action by OrangeLLM or any superstack LLM passes through a Hermes lease — allowedActions, forbiddenActions, riskLevel, expiry. Eight LOOM gates must pass before any action lands.

instruction: What is Mirage?
output: Mirage is the data + memory plane of Orange5. It has two adapter families: mirage/data/* for external mounts (postgres, drive, gmail, slack, github, redis — 11 mounts total) and mirage/memory/* for internal stores (Flux ledgers, Graph Weaver typed graph, receipts). Same query shape; only mirage/data/* writes need operator approval per call.

instruction: What is AtomSmasher?
output: AtomSmasher is the compression and compiler module suite of Orange5. Twelve modules: Commitment Atoms, AIR Codec, EquationStore, Cartridges, Sparse Worksets, Least-action Router, Expansion Warrants, Compression Debt Ledger, Saved Work Certificates, Canon Pressure Detector, Pathwave Compressor, Anti-fluff Gate. Currently only the Anti-fluff Gate is LIVE; the rest are STUB until promoted per the COLAB_TRAINING_PATTERN.

instruction: What is ToolMesh?
output: ToolMesh is the 11-lab capability layer under OrangeLLM. Image, video, audio, design, coding, automation, analytics, public-agent, observability, security, releaseops. Each lab holds tool-cards OrangeLLM consults before requesting operator approval. Tool-cards are capability indicators, not permission-to-execute.

instruction: What is Mom's Law?
output: Mom's Law is the meta-law that sits above all other Orange5 doctrine: give full effort every time. Every response, every line of code, every receipt earns its place. No coasting. No theater. No 'this part doesn't matter.' Mom is watching every output. If any rule conflicts with Mom's Law, Mom's Law wins and the other rule changes.

instruction: What is the Frontier-Isolation Law?
output: The frontier model hosted inside Atomic Orange (Opus 4.7, Gemini, GPT-5.5, GLM, MiniMax — whatever BYO key the operator brings) talks only to OrangeLLM at 127.0.0.1:1337/v1. It never reaches Orange5 internals: not Mirage mounts, not the command server at :8787, not Smart Skinny at :8797, not the Codexa rail, not the file system. OrangeLLM filters what the frontier sees. This makes BYO-key frontier integration safe by design.

instruction: What is the Codeless Law?
output: No code editor surface inside Atomic Orange. No IDE lane. No Monaco. No Tab autocomplete. No Agent Mode hotkey. No repo indexer. Orange5 is operator + chat + OrangeLLM doing the thinking + Hermes doing the work. Files are edited externally; the cockpit surface is for command, memory, and observation only.

instruction: What is the LLM-Over-Agent Law?
output: LLMs sit above agents in the Orange5 hierarchy. Every LLM in the model superstack can spawn its own Hermes-leased agents. Agents do not spawn LLMs. The PM brain delegates with explicit leases; the lease is the agent's authority.

instruction: What is the OrangeLLM-Is-The-Gateway Law?
output: OrangeLLM plus Flow Direct is the only path to the model superstack, the tools (Mirage, AtomSmasher, ToolMesh), and the visual capability. Nothing else reaches them directly. The gateway at 127.0.0.1:1337 enforces this with the 16-fixture boundary middleware.

instruction: What are the four Orange5 laws in order?
output: 1) Frontier-Isolation Law: frontier touches only OrangeLLM, never Orange5 internals. 2) LLM-Over-Agent Law: LLMs spawn agents under Hermes leases. 3) OrangeLLM-Is-The-Gateway Law: only path to superstack, tools, and visual. 4) Codeless Law: no IDE, no editor, no autocomplete at the operator surface.

instruction: What is composition-AGI?
output: Composition-AGI is the Orange5 architectural doctrine: an operator-leverage AI built as a constellation of specialized small models, each constrained at the logit level (GBNF, JSON Schema, etc.) so each organ cannot lie outside its lane. Coordinated by a PM brain (OrangeLLM). The opposite of scaling one giant LLM until it can do everything.

All actions traverse this stack in ~200ms before they land. Gate 0 cannot be bypassed.

instruction: What is the orange.order.v1 schema?
output: The orange.order.v1 JSON schema is what OrangeLLM emits before any action. Required fields: schema (const orange.order.v1), orderId (min 3 chars), intent, scope, allowedActions (string[]), forbiddenActions (string[]), targetProject, riskLevel (enum read_only|low|medium|high|destructive|production), requiresReceipt (bool). Lives at 09-SCHEMAS/orange.order.v1.schema.json.

instruction: What is the orange.report.v1 schema?
output: The orange.report.v1 JSON schema is what OrangeLLM emits after any action. Required fields: schema (const orange.report.v1), orderId, status, confidence (0-1), actionsTaken, evidence, blockers, nextAction, receiptPath. Lives at 09-SCHEMAS/orange.report.v1.schema.json.

instruction: What is the AgentTurn JSON schema?
output: AgentTurn is Æ Cobra's GBNF-locked output shape. Required fields: lane (reality|thought|merge), event_type (observation|decision|error|checkpoint|recall|receipt|risk), summary, entities (string[]), files (string[]), commands (string[]), risk (low|medium|high), next_action, confidence (0-1). The grammar prevents any prose outside this shape at the logit level.

instruction: What is AECode?
output: AECode is the canonical source contract of Orange5. The intent → AECode Source → mission contract → target plan → isolated patch/artifact → gauntlet → receipt → approval pipeline. AECode is the middle voice between human intent and any specific output language (TypeScript, Rust, Python, etc.).

instruction: What is AELang?
output: AELang v0.1 is the two-tier route language of Orange5. AELang-High (human-readable intent) → AELang-Core (machine-parseable) → ORANGEBOX Route Packet. Operates under departments AE0-AE14 with route-first, receipt-first, visual-first discipline.

instruction: What is a hash chain in Orange5 receipts?
output: Every receipt at 10-RECEIPTS/orange5-build/ carries a prior_receipt field pointing at the previous receipt's id, plus its own SHA-256 hash. If any receipt mid-chain is tampered with, every downstream prior_receipt breaks. Tamper-evident audit trail. The chain is currently at #013 (the 1-tier-architecture-locked receipt).

instruction: Where does OrangeLLM-fatty serve its OpenAI-compatible endpoint?
output: 127.0.0.1:1337/v1 (the OrangeLLM gateway). The frontier model in Atomic Orange and any external tool reaches OrangeLLM only here. The gateway proxies to the actual model running on Codexa via the rail.

instruction: Where does Æ Cobra serve its daemon?
output: 127.0.0.1:7419 (loopback inside Codexa WSL2). Reachable from N150 only via the Codexa command rail at 10.0.99.1:8097/api/ae-cobra/ with the rail token. Never exposed directly to non-loopback.

instruction: Where does Qdrant live in Orange5?
output: Codexa Docker container aeorangebox-ai-box-qdrant-1 at port 6333. Kept from the legacy Orange stack because OrangeEye uses it for ColBERT-style MaxSim retrieval over multi-vector patch embeddings. Collection name: orange5-vision.

instruction: What is the dedicated Flux mount on Codexa?
output: /mnt/ae_flux (inside WSL2). Holds events/{reality,thought,merge}, index/* binary sidecars, state/* SSM checkpoints, receipts/, logs/, tmp/. Either on a dedicated NVMe partition (preferred) or a Windows-mounted folder via WSL2 (Night-1 fallback).

instruction: What is the difference between Reality lane and Thought lane in Æ Cobra?
output: Reality lane records immutable ground truth from origin sources: terminal stdout, Hermes execution receipts, Mirage observations, OrangeEye screenshots, operator input. Thought lane records hypotheses, plans, rejected branches, OrangeLLM reasoning traces. When the two contradict, Reality always wins; the conflict surfaces in StateBrief output.

instruction: How does Æ Cobra decide lane assignment?
output: Origin-based, not string-match. The event SOURCE determines the lane: terminal → Reality, Hermes receipt → Reality, OrangeEye → Reality, operator input → Reality, OrangeLLM reasoning → Thought, OrangeLLM rejected candidate → Thought. The model never decides its own lane; the caller (Bun Flow Direct) sets it based on which subsystem produced the event. This kills the V1 string-match blind spot at design time.

instruction: What is the V1 vulnerability in Æ Cobra and how is it mitigated?
output: V1: a string-match classifier would misroute ground-truth events into the Thought lane if the event text contained Thought-keyword tokens like 'plan' or 'maybe' — for example a terminal output reading 'error: failed to load plan'. V1 is mitigated at design time by using origin-based lane assignment from Day One: the caller sets the lane based on the event source subsystem, never on event text content.

instruction: What is the V2 vulnerability in Æ Cobra and how is it mitigated?
output: V2: Q5 quantization floating-point error can accumulate during checkpoint-replay reconstruction of the SSM hidden state, causing drift from the original runtime state. V2 is mitigated by recording a state_hash at every checkpoint; on replay-to-target, the hash is recomputed and compared. If drift exceeds the threshold, the recall is refused or falls back to the next-later checkpoint. No silent drift past threshold.

instruction: What is the GBNF grammar lock in Æ Cobra?
output: agent_turn.gbnf is loaded into llama.cpp at server startup. It constrains the model's logit space such that the model can only emit JSON matching the AgentTurn schema — no prose, no markdown, no roleplay can exit. Bullshit is impossible at the output layer, not just at the parser layer.

instruction: What is CLR in Æ Cobra?
output: Claim-Level Reliability. K candidate AgentTurns are generated for each event; each is scored on grounded files, grounded commands, confidence, and risk-vs-content sanity. Night-1: K=1 with anti-fluff and grounding check. Phase-5: K=5 with claim verification against Reality lane and Hermes receipts. Threshold 0.50; below threshold = reject + write rejection receipt to Thought lane.

instruction: What is mlock and why does Æ Cobra use it?
output: mlock pins the Mamba model weights in physical RAM, preventing the Linux kernel from paging them to disk. Combined with --no-mmap, this guarantees the resident daemon stays in memory with VmSwap=0 and predictable inference latency. Critical for the 10 GB software ceiling discipline on Codexa.

instruction: Why Mamba SSM instead of a transformer for Æ Cobra?
output: Transformer KV cache grows linearly with context; sustained operation blows past the 10 GB ceiling and triggers OS swap, destroying latency. Mamba's fixed-size hidden state means the recurrent memory stays the same size regardless of how much history the daemon processes. The only mathematical way to keep the daemon resident long-term.

instruction: What quantization does Æ Cobra use?
output: Q5_K_M default for strict JSON validity (~2.6 GB). Q4_K_M fallback only if Q5 latency is unacceptable AND JSON validity stays ≥95%. Q3, Q2, Q8 are forbidden for the daemon role.

instruction: What is the Schism Engine in Æ Cobra?
output: The Schism Engine is the dual-stream memory architecture: Reality lane and Thought lane as separate hash-chained ledgers on dedicated NVMe. Reality is immutable ground truth; Thought is hypothesis. Reality always wins on conflict. Phase-4 promotes this to dual recurrent SSM states (Reality.state and Thought.state) with state_fork and state_merge primitives.

instruction: What is Flux in Orange5?
output: Flux is the SSD ledger system. Append-only JSONL records during Night-1, with binary Rust packets in Phase-3. Files: reality.flux, thought.flux, merge.flux on /mnt/ae_flux. Each record carries prev_hash and hash for tamper-evident chain. Binary sidecar .idx files give O(1) random-access by timestamp.

instruction: What is a StateBrief?
output: StateBrief is what Mirage returns when OrangeLLM asks for memory recall. JSON with: query, time_range, reality (array of cited reality events), thought (array of cited thought events), conflicts (where the two differ with resolution), recommended_next_action, confidence. Reality always overrides Thought. Receipts override recollection.

instruction: Where does OrangeLLM query for memory?
output: POST 127.0.0.1:1337/v1/memory/state-brief with a JSON body containing query, optional time_range, optional lanes filter, max_records, include_conflicts. The gateway routes the query to Mirage which reads Flux + Graph + (if needed) external Mirage-Data mounts. Frontier models never reach this endpoint directly.

instruction: What is the Graph Weaver?
output: The Graph Weaver is the semantic indexer that runs as a background daemon on Codexa, tail-watching reality.flux and thought.flux. For each new Flux record, it extracts typed entities via qwen3:0.6b on N150 and writes typed nodes + edges to SQLite at 06-ORANGELLM/memory/graph.db. Receipts override recollection; the graph cross-references back into Flux via receipt_ids.

instruction: What is the 10-node 6-edge ontology of the Graph Weaver?
output: Nodes: Sovereign, Project, Mission, Lane, Model, Tool, Service, Host, Receipt, Doctrine. Edges: PROVES, REQUIRES, BLOCKED_BY, SUPERSEDES, APPROVED_BY, OBSERVED_BY. Locked core ontology — new types only via receipt-gated extension protocol (≥5 receipts referencing a candidate OR explicit operator promotion).

instruction: What is the OrangeEye Eye layer?
output: ColQwen2.5 (or ColPali-3 when available) running on Codexa CPU + NPU via OpenVINO. Encodes each image or PDF page into 196 visual patch embeddings of 128-dim Int8, no OCR. Output: ~100 KB per page including metadata. The model is loaded on-demand for ingestion batches, then unloaded to save RAM.

instruction: What is MaxSim in OrangeEye?
output: ColBERT-style late-interaction scoring. For a query q and document d, S(q,d) = Σ_i max_j (E_q(i) · E_d(j)), where E_q(i) is the i-th query token embedding and E_d(j) is the j-th visual patch embedding. Qdrant supports this natively via multi_vector_config with comparator=max_sim. Preserves spatial coordinates of the matching patch — OrangeLLM gets the answer with x,y coordinates intact.

instruction: What is GLM-4.6V in Orange5?
output: GLM-4.6V is the Phase-1 OrangeEye edge cortex. ~8 GB at Q4, served via Ollama on Codexa, ~3-10s per query on CPU + Vulkan iGPU offload. Three operations: /v1/visual/describe (image Q&A), /v1/visual/extract-structure (table/chart/form/ui-mock parsing), /v1/visual/ground-ui (find element coords from intent).

instruction: When does OrangeEye offload to the frontier model?
output: Four conditions trigger frontier offload: (1) local edge cortex confidence below 0.7, (2) operator explicit /deep flag in the query, (3) image or video exceeds the local model's token budget, (4) layout complexity exceeds the patch-grid resolution. The offload routes through the gateway with the operator's BYO key; Frontier-Isolation Law preserves the boundary.

instruction: Why is OrangeEye not the 5th pillar?
output: OrangeEye is a tier under OrangeLLM, not a peer pillar. The pillars are the four cognitive organs: Orange5 (system), Atomic Orange (UI), OrangeLLM (PM brain), AE Flow (runtime). Vision is a sense, not a thinker — it translates pixels to structured text that OrangeLLM acts on. Demoted in the 2026-06-23 spec rewrite.

instruction: What is MiniEyes?
output: MiniEyes is the addendum visual model — a 2-8B local VLM custom-trained on Orange5 dashboard screenshots, AECode diagrams, and receipts. Built ONLY if the primary visual stack (GLM-4.6V + Playwright MCP + Chrome DevTools + UX tools) proves insufficient under real load. Optional, deferred to Phase-3+.

instruction: What is a current in AE Flow?
output: A current is an open task or pressure flow in the Flow runtime. Each current carries a pressure value (0..1 normalized), owner_department (AE0-AE14), status (pending|in_progress|awaiting_approval|closed|blocked|escalated), assigned_agent, acceptance criteria, and timestamps. High-pressure currents win attention on each tick.

instruction: What is an agent in AE Flow?
output: An agent is a worker that rides a current. Each agent has a role (orangellm-light, orangellm-heavy, codexa-rail, etc.), state (idle|riding|cooling), the current_id it's currently riding, and capability (lane: reflex|heavy|visual|agentic|...). Agents are assigned to pending currents in pressure order each tick.

instruction: What is a delta in AE Flow?
output: A delta is what actually changed in the last tick. Kinds: current_pressure_change, agent_assigned, agent_released, current_closed, current_blocked, governor_throttled. The Cockpit lane shows deltas as they land — visible state-change events, not log spam. The most recent 500 deltas are retained in the state file.

instruction: What is a governor in AE Flow?
output: A governor is a backpressure rule. Examples: concurrency_cap (cap simultaneous in_progress currents and throttle the lowest-pressure overflow), escalate (move a stuck current to escalated state), block (transition to blocked with reason). Governors evaluate every tick after agent assignment.

instruction: What is the AE Flow tick loop?
output: Each tick: (1) assignAgents — give idle agents to highest-pressure pending currents matching their lane; (2) evaluate governors and apply actions; (3) emit deltas to the state file; (4) persist state to JSON snapshot at 05-FLOW/state/flow.json (SQLite migration in PR-10). Tick count and last_tick_at are persisted with the state.

instruction: How does a current close in AE Flow?
output: closeCurrent(state, current_id, {receipt_path}) requires a receipt_path when current.acceptance.receipt_required is true (default). Sets status=closed, closed_at=now, closed_receipt=receipt_path, releases the riding agent back to idle, and emits a current_closed delta. Without the receipt, the call throws — no fake-green closure possible.

instruction: How do I start the OrangeLLM gateway?
output: From Windows PowerShell: cd C:\AtomEons\Orange5\06-ORANGELLM, then node server\index.mjs. The server binds 127.0.0.1:1337 only (loopback enforced — never 0.0.0.0). Successful start prints 'orangellm listening on 127.0.0.1:1337 (orange5.orangellm.v0.3.0-pr03)' and 'frontier-isolation law active'.

instruction: How do I check OrangeLLM gateway health?
output: curl http://127.0.0.1:1337/healthz . Returns JSON with: status (ok|degraded|down), service, version, boundary (frontier_isolation_active), upstream (smart_skinny and fatty live/dead), routes (allowed paths and the law). If upstream.smart_skinny.live is false, the chat lane returns 502/503 until Smart Skinny is started.

instruction: What are the allowed endpoints on the OrangeLLM gateway?
output: Exactly three: GET /healthz, GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions. Anything else returns 404. Path-traversal patterns (..), forbidden prefixes (/api, /admin, /cmd, /exec, /shell, /fs, /mirage, /codexa, /orangebox, /hermes, /vault) return 403. Forbidden headers (X-Mirage-, X-Orangebox-, X-Codexa-, X-Internal-) return 403. The boundary holds 16/16 in fixtures.

instruction: What size limit does the gateway impose on request bodies?
output: 1 MB cap (1_000_000 bytes). Anything larger has the connection destroyed mid-stream. Prevents abuse and keeps the daemon responsive.

instruction: How does Atomic Orange route between lanes?
output: React Router 7 BrowserRouter. Routes: / redirects to /chat, /chat (Chat lane), /cockpit (Cockpit), /vault (Vault), /settings (Settings). Vision Rail uses NavLink to highlight the active lane. Keyboard: not exposed via hotkey in the React shell directly, but Tauri can wire Ctrl+1..4 in src-tauri.

instruction: Where does Atomic Orange store local settings?
output: window.localStorage under key 'atomic-orange.settings'. Includes brainTier (reflex|heavy|frontier), forceOrangeOrders (bool), orangeIndicator (bool), customRule (string), apiKey (BYO frontier key — local only, password input), egressMode (locked|byo-key|dev). Auto-persists on every change.

instruction: What does the Cockpit lane in Atomic Orange show?
output: Live polling of /healthz and /v1/models every 4 seconds. Cards for Gateway (service, version, status, boundary), Upstream Smart Skinny (state), Upstream Fatty (state), Models served (id, lane, state, upstream details). Operator sees memory freshness, drift, hardware utilization on the same surface — the AESee Suite Lite.

instruction: What does the Vault lane do?
output: Drag-drop a PDF or image; ColPali ingests; Qdrant MaxSim retrieves; GLM-4.6V (or frontier offload if complex) grounds the answer. Returns top-K pages with patch coordinates and inline citations. Plus K3 wildcard memory queries — alias, lexical, authority, Cold Truth Gate. Stale memory survives offline via cockpit shadow cache.

instruction: What does the Settings lane control?
output: Brain tier selector (segmented control: reflex|heavy|frontier), gateway endpoint info, custom assistant rule editor, force-Orange-orders toggle, Orange running indicator toggle, BYO frontier API key (password input, local only), Mirage mount permissions, egress mode (locked|byo-key|dev), Save local profile button.

instruction: What is the /orange shortcut in Atomic Orange?
output: A chat command that forces the current chat to route through OrangeLLM regardless of which frontier model is selected. Useful when the operator wants the trained PM brain to handle a query specifically. Combined with the 'force every chat to call OrangeLLM' Settings toggle for default sticky behavior.

instruction: What is custom-rule stickiness in Atomic Orange?
output: A markdown rule the operator writes in the Settings lane that gets included in every chat prompt's system role. Stored in localStorage. Drop rules/*.md files in a future watched folder to add additional rules. Gateway-side rule-file syncing is a backend lane not yet wired.

instruction: What is the Orange running indicator?
output: A live pulse in the Atomic Orange chrome bar (or status pill) that shows when OrangeLLM is actively processing. Breathes orange when thinking, glows green when idle, pulses red when health is degraded. Toggleable in Settings under 'orangeIndicator'.

instruction: What is the 1-tier trained architecture decision?
output: Locked 2026-06-24 by operator. One trained PM brain — OrangeLLM-fatty (qwen3:30b-a3b Q4 + Orange5 LoRA) — on Codexa. N150 holds stock qwen3:0.6b + nomic-embed-text for utility (lane classifier, embedder, emergency fallback chat) but no custom LoRA. Smart Skinny custom training lane retired.

instruction: Why kill Smart Skinny custom LoRA?
output: Two trained tiers means two adapters to maintain, two bakeoffs, two promotion gates, two corpus pipelines, and the risk of canonical drift between them. One trained brain = one promotion lane = simpler ops surface for the solo operator. N150's role becomes utility-only with stock weights — no training maintenance there. Codexa carries the trained mind.

No trained models live here.

instruction: What runs on Codexa in Orange5 (full deployment)?
output: OrangeLLM-fatty (qwen3:30b-a3b + Orange5 LoRA, ~20 GB), Æ Cobra Mamba 2.8B Q5 daemon (~3 GB mlock), GLM-4.6V Q4 visual cortex (~8 GB on-demand), ColPali Q4 ingestion (~5 GB on-demand), embedder (~0.5 GB), Bun Flow Direct + Rust Flux Engine daemons in WSL2, Qdrant Docker container, Graph Weaver background indexer. Allows the N150 cockpit to invoke read-only and allowlisted-mutation commands on Codexa: ops-readiness, system-check, health-report, project-report, reality-watch, model-inventory, trilane-doctor, ipi-doctor, memory-doctor, mcp-doctor. instruction: What is a promotion gate?
output: Logic that decides promote / hold / reject for any candidate change. Required inputs: receipt_path, bakeoff result, status, risk_level. Auto-rejects if status contains fake-green words (green_assumed, looks_ok, probably, should_work, fake_green). Auto-holds if missing receipt_path or missing bakeoff. Requires operator_approved=true for risk_level in [high, destructive, production]. Lives at 04-CONTROL-PLANE/src/promotion-gate.mjs.

instruction: What is the Anti-fluff Gate in AtomSmasher?
output: A regex-based check that flags verbose, hedged, or theater language in model output. Patterns: 'in summary', 'to summarize', 'it is important to note', 'I hope this helps', 'might/maybe/perhaps', 'seems to/appears to/kind of'. Verdict: pass (0 hits), warn (1-2 hits), reject (3+ hits). The only currently-LIVE AtomSmasher module — the other 11 are STUB.

instruction: What is a Hermes lease?
output: A bounded execution contract. Fields: id, actor (which LLM holds it), allowed (action verbs the agent may perform), forbidden (verbs blocked — default forbidden auto-merged: destructive_write, production_deploy, scope_expansion, egress_unbounded), targetProject, riskLevel, expires_at, requires_approval. checkAction enforces every proposed action against the lease.

instruction: What are the 8 LOOM gates?
output: order_schema (order matches orange.order.v1), report_schema (report matches orange.report.v1), receipt_spine (receipt_path exists), human_approval (if lease.requires_approval, operator approved), codexa_lease (lease present), openai_gateway (gateway-mediated), mcp_default (default MCP handshake), false_green_guard (no fake-green words in status). All 8 must pass for an action to land. Lives at 08-HERMES/src/loom-gates.mjs.

instruction: What is the Frontier-Isolation boundary middleware?
output: Lives at 06-ORANGELLM/server/boundary.mjs. Enforces: only GET /healthz, GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions are reachable. Path-traversal patterns rejected with 403. Forbidden path prefixes rejected with 403. Forbidden header prefixes (X-Mirage-, X-Orangebox-, X-Codexa-, X-Internal-) rejected with 403. Authorization must be Bearer if present. Body size capped at 1 MB. 16 boundary fixtures pass; 12 reject cases all return correct status.

instruction: What is the cockpit shadow cache?
output: A recent-events mirror of reality.flux + thought.flux from Codexa, synced hourly to the N150 cockpit at 06-ORANGELLM/memory/cache/. When the Codexa rail is down (401, network drop, etc.), Atomic Orange's Vault lane queries the shadow cache instead — stale memory is better than no memory. Cockpit dash shows last sync time + drift since.

instruction: What is the bakeoff in Orange5 model promotion?
output: A 5-dimension head-to-head eval. Dimensions: mission-shape (emits valid orange.report.v1), doctrine-recall (cites 27 Guardrails, AE0-AE14, 9-Gate correctly), topology-recall (ports, hosts, configs accurate), receipt-grounding (cites real receipts), refusal-discipline (refuses out-of-scope and forbidden actions). New candidate must win ≥4 of 5 dimensions vs baseline to promote. Operator approval required for risk_level ≥ high.

instruction: What is the corpus assembly stage of a training pass?
output: Stage 1 of the Colab Training Pattern. A Workflow agent on Codexa reads relevant reality.flux + thought.flux + receipts + doctrine docs, synthesizes instruction-tuning JSONL pairs ({instruction, input, output}), validates against the training-corpus.v0 schema, writes to 16-TRAINING/corpus/<model-name>-v<N>.jsonl with SHA-256 captured in receipt.

instruction: What is the config generation stage of a training pass?
output: Stage 2. A Workflow agent picks Axolotl as default (or Unsloth if base supports it), generates a YAML config tuned to the Colab GPU tier (T4/V100/A100), sets epoch count, learning rate, LoRA rank/alpha based on model size, and emits a paired .ipynb Colab notebook. Output: 16-TRAINING/configs/<model-name>-v<N>.yaml + .ipynb.

instruction: What is the Colab tier needed for OrangeLLM-fatty v0 training?

instruction: What is the lane discriminator in Æ Cobra?
output: The function that decides whether an incoming event lands in reality.flux or thought.flux. Origin-based (V1 mitigation): terminal stdout → reality, Hermes execution receipt → reality, Mirage observation → reality, OrangeEye screenshot → reality, OrangeLLM reasoning trace → thought, OrangeLLM rejected candidate → thought. The Bun Flow Direct caller sets the lane; the daemon never decides its own lane.

instruction: Why is the lane classifier origin-based and not string-match?
output: String-match would misroute. Example: a terminal output 'error: failed to load plan' contains the word 'plan' — a string-match classifier would tag it Thought lane (since 'plan' is a Thought-keyword). But it's literal terminal stdout: ground truth, Reality lane. Origin-based decides from the event SOURCE (terminal subsystem produced it), not from event content. This is the V1 vulnerability mitigation.

instruction: What is the lane mapping table for Æ Cobra Day-One classifier?
output: Terminal stdout/stderr → reality. Hermes execution receipt → reality. Mirage data plane read → reality. OrangeEye screenshot/DOM/UI → reality. Compiler/build output → reality. OrangeLLM reasoning trace → thought. OrangeLLM rejected candidate → thought. Operator chat input raw → reality. Operator decision/approval/rejection → reality. Strategy/pivot/scope proposal → thought. Merge synthesis between Reality + Thought → merge.

instruction: What is the chat-to-flux pipeline?
output: One operator turn produces 4-8 Flux events. Operator types message → Reality (origin=ui, kind=observation). OrangeLLM reasoning trace → Thought (sampled, kind=decision). OrangeLLM calls Hermes → Reality (origin=hermes, kind=receipt). Hermes result → Reality (origin=hermes, kind=receipt). File diff → Reality (origin=terminal, kind=diff). OrangeLLM final reply → Reality (origin=orange, kind=observation). Rejected candidate → Thought (kind=decision).

instruction: How are Hermes receipts double-written?
output: Every Hermes execution receipt lands as two artifacts: a Markdown audit file at 10-RECEIPTS/orange5-build/<timestamp>-<action>.md AND a hash-chained JSONL record at /mnt/ae_flux/events/reality/<date>.jsonl. Same event, two representations, same SHA-256 for cross-reference. Human audit + machine audit.

instruction: How does OrangeLLM auto-inject memory each turn?
output: Per the hybrid coupling pattern (Option C from spec): every chat completion auto-injects a 'recent context' StateBrief into the system role — last 5 reality events + last 3 thought events + any open conflicts. Plus operator/model can emit a <recall>{query}</recall> tag mid-turn that triggers a deeper Mirage StateBrief query. The recall result lands as [MEMORY:RECALLED] system message with precedence label.

instruction: What does [MEMORY:RECALLED] mean in OrangeLLM prompts?
output: A precedence label wrapping injected memory: '[MEMORY:RECALLED] (this is verified history from Æ Cobra Flux. Reality cites > Thought cites. Receipts > recollection.) {state_brief_json} [END:RECALLED]'. Tells the model the content inside is authoritative history, not user input or hallucination. Without this label OrangeLLM might dismiss memory or hallucinate around it.

instruction: What is the orange5-vision Qdrant collection?
output: The multi-vector store for OrangeEye Phase-1. Vector config: 128-dim, dot distance, multivector_config.comparator=max_sim, datatype=uint8 (Int8 quantized patches). Indexed payload: source (path/URL), page (int), doc_id (sha256), ingested_at, lane (doc|ui-screenshot|video-frame|chart|whiteboard). Storage: ~100 KB per page; ~1 GB at 10K pages; ~100 GB at 1M pages.

instruction: What does OrangeEye write to Reality lane?
output: Every cortex query produces a Reality-lane Flux event with kind=observation, plus an ae_visual block: {image_sha256, qdrant_doc_id, patch_grounding (array of {idx, bbox, conf}), cortex_model (e.g. glm-4.6v), frontier_used (bool)}. Three weeks later OrangeLLM can ask 'what did we see on Tuesday' and get a StateBrief with patch coordinates still attached.

instruction: What are the four conditions that trigger frontier offload from OrangeEye?
output: (1) local edge cortex confidence < 0.7. (2) operator explicit /deep flag. (3) image or video exceeds local token budget. (4) layout complexity exceeds patch-grid resolution. When any fires, query routes via 127.0.0.1:1337 to the operator's BYO frontier (Opus, Gemini, GPT, GLM, MiniMax) — Frontier-Isolation Law preserved.

instruction: How does ColPali ingestion work in detail?
output: For each input image or PDF page: ColQwen2.5 encodes it into 196 visual patches arranged in a 14×14 grid. Each patch becomes a 128-dim Int8 embedding (~25 KB raw, ~100 KB with metadata). Total per page: model + tokenizer + grid layout = ~500ms-2s on Codexa CPU. Output streamed to Qdrant upsert. Model unloaded between ingestion batches to save 5 GB RAM.

instruction: How does MaxSim retrieval work in OrangeEye?
output: Operator query → ColQwen2.5 embeds the query text into N token vectors. Qdrant scans the orange5-vision collection. For each document d with patches P, score = Σ_i max_p∈P (E_q(i) · E_d(p)). Return top-K documents with patch indices of the matching patches. Patch indices → bbox coordinates → OrangeLLM asks the cortex 'describe the region at coordinates X' for grounding.

instruction: What happens to vision queries when Codexa is unreachable?
output: The gateway returns 502 upstream_unreachable. The operator's Vault lane shows the error inline. The cockpit shadow cache may still serve PREVIOUSLY-INGESTED documents from N150's mirror of recent Flux events, but no NEW ingestion is possible without Codexa. Phase-2: explicit offline mode could route to frontier-only if operator's BYO key is set.

instruction: How does Atomic Orange handle the frontier model swap?
output: Settings lane → Frontier key field (password input). Operator pastes BYO key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, z.ai, MiniMax). Chat lane sends requests with Authorization: Bearer <key>. Gateway forwards the Bearer token through to OrangeLLM, which uses it for frontier offload calls. Key never persists outside Atomic Orange's localStorage.

instruction: What is the visible-reasoning policy in Orange5?
output: Disabled by default. The PM brain shows final reply, not chain-of-thought. Per the Atomic Orange Model Lane Contract — visible reasoning is a debugging tool, not a UX default. Operators can opt-in via Settings if they want to see OrangeLLM's reasoning trace. The reasoning still lands in Thought-lane Flux records either way for audit.

instruction: How do you write a green Orange5 receipt?
output: Eight rules: (1) Include receipt_id, generated_at, schema, hash_chain integer. (2) prior_receipt must match the predecessor receipt's id (chain integrity). (3) status must NOT contain fake-green words (looks_ok, probably, should_work, green_assumed). (4) confidence is a real 0..1 number, not always 1.0. (5) actions taken include EVERY action, including failed ones. (6) evidence cites real files, real commands, real outputs. (7) blockers are named, not omitted. (8) next_action is concrete and small.

instruction: What makes a receipt rejected by the promotion gate?
output: Any of: (a) missing receipt_path; (b) missing bakeoff result; (c) bakeoff result = fail; (d) status contains any forbidden fake-green word; (e) risk_level in [high, destructive, production] without operator_approved=true. The gate returns 'promote', 'hold', or 'reject' — hold for remediable issues, reject for terminal.

instruction: What is a rollback receipt?
output: A receipt written when an action is undone. Includes original receipt_id (the one being rolled back), the rollback command run, the rollback verification, and the new system state. The hash chain continues — rollback receipts are part of the same chain. Mom's Law: no silent rollback; the rollback itself leaves a trace.

instruction: How does Hermes refuse a destructive action?
output: checkAction(lease, action, {operator_approved}) returns {allowed: false, reason: 'action_forbidden:<verb>' | 'operator_approval_required' | 'lease_expired' | 'action_not_in_allowlist'}. The Hermes daemon writes a rejection receipt to thought.flux with kind=risk, includes the proposed action, the lease state, and the refusal reason. OrangeLLM sees the refusal in the next memory injection — learning not to propose it again.

instruction: What is the operator's role per training pass?
output: Five steps, ~5 minutes hands-on total. Receive notification from Workflow tool. Open Colab in browser. Upload the generated .ipynb. Click Runtime → Run all. Walk away. The rest is GPU compute + Workflow agents retrieving the adapter + bakeoff + receipt. Total operator time per pass: under 10 minutes.

instruction: What does qwen3:0.6b do on the N150?

(2) Emergency chat reflex fallback — when Codexa rail is down or slow, N150 serves a degraded chat experience locally via stock Ollama. Both jobs work with stock weights — no LoRA, no bakeoff.

instruction: What does nomic-embed-text do on the N150?

For each new Flux record entity extraction, nomic-embed-text produces a 768-dim vector that lands in the SQLite graph node's optional embedding column for semantic recall. ~50ms per text. Stock model — no custom training. Could also be hosted on Codexa via Ollama for offload but N150 latency is preferable.

instruction: How does the operator add a new doctrine type to the Graph Weaver ontology?

(2) Candidate lands in 06-ORANGELLM/memory/ontology-candidates.jsonl with a counter and at least one referencing receipt. (3) Promotion triggers when ≥5 receipts reference it across ≥2 missions OR operator types 'promote-ontology <name>'. (4) Schema bumps (ontology.v1 → v2) with a migration receipt and graph rewrite from tag-strings to typed nodes.

instruction: What is the Operator SOP for a typical session?
output: Ten steps: (1) Open chat in Atomic Orange. (2) State objective. (3) OrangeLLM compiles orange.order.v1; if risk≥high routes to approval gate. (4) OrangeLLM picks worker (cockpit|codexa) and lane (reflex|local-fast|local-code|subscription-frontier|tool-execution); patches in ghost worktree. (5) OrangeLLM runs doctor + gauntlet + smoke. instruction: What is the 12-gate top-of-model health check?

Gates include: Orange5 lane is present, doctrine corpus is loaded, receipts directory is writeable, hash chain is intact, no orphaned currents in AE Flow, Æ Cobra heartbeat is fresh, OrangeLLM gateway returns 200, boundary fixtures still 16/16, no fake-green words in recent receipts, Hermes leases haven't expired, ontology candidates queue isn't overflowing, recent training receipt verifies promotion.

instruction: What is the daily continuity packet?

Lands in Reality-lane Flux. Becomes the first context injection of the next session — Mirage auto-pulls the most recent continuity packet on chat start.

instruction: What is the AECommander Extract pattern?

instruction: What is the receipt-gated ontology extension protocol?

instruction: What kills a heavy operation in Orange5?

instruction: How does AE Flow persist state?
output: Night-1: JSON snapshot at 05-FLOW/state/flow.json, written atomically every tick. Delta tail trimmed to MAX_DELTAS=500 to bound file size. State includes currents (Object), agents (Object), deltas (Array), tick (int), last_tick_at (timestamp). Phase-3: SQLite migration to 06-CONTROL-PLANE/receipts/orange5.db with proper transactions and indexes.

instruction: What is the AE Flow concurrency_cap?
output: A governor parameter limiting how many currents can be in_progress simultaneously. Default 3. Overflow currents (lowest pressure) get throttled — agent released, current reverts to pending. The governor_throttled delta records the reason ('concurrency cap N exceeded'). Operator can set via runtime config.

instruction: What is the orange5-vision lane field used for?

The plugin lives as 07-SKILLS/ae0-factory-plugin/ as historical reference; Orange5 routes through OrangeLLM's trained brain instead of the plugin.

instruction: What is operator-grade refusal in Orange5?
output: OrangeLLM refuses to: (1) act outside scope, (2) act without a receipt, (3) ship a claim without grounding, (4) bypass operator approval on risk≥high, (5) fabricate file paths or commands, (6) emit prose-heavy reasoning when AgentTurn shape is required, (7) ignore Mom's Law, (8) lie about heavy lane availability when it's down. Each refusal writes a Thought-lane receipt explaining the rejection.

instruction: What is the difference between confidence 0.5 and confidence 0.9 in an AgentTurn?
output: Confidence is a calibrated estimate of the AgentTurn's correctness. 0.9+ = grounded in observed event, files/commands verified, low ambiguity. 0.5-0.8 = inferred from context, some assumptions, partial grounding. 0.2-0.5 = significant uncertainty, multiple plausible readings. <0.2 = the daemon refuses. instruction: What is QLoRA?
output: Quantized LoRA. The base model loads in 4-bit (NF4 quantization) which dramatically reduces VRAM usage. Then LoRA adapter weights train in higher precision (typically bf16). Lets a 30B model train on a V100 16GB or A100 40GB that couldn't hold the full 30B at fp16. Adapter is small (~80-150 MB for 30B), separable, swappable. Promoted-into-production via Ollama Modelfile merge.
